words.enDefinition: a question directed to a particular student without advance notice at the start of a case discussion

examples.en: The lecturer used an opening cold call to ask which option the shop should choose.
examples.zh: 讲师用一次「开场点名提问」问那家店该选哪个方案。

examples.en: I prepared my recommendation in case I got the opening cold call in our seminar.
examples.zh: 我准备好了自己的建议，以防研讨课「开场点名提问」叫到我。

collocations: start with an opening cold call
prepare for the opening cold call

words.enDefinition: a written or recorded account of a situation created for learners to analyse and discuss

examples.en: The teaching case described a bicycle shop trying to serve two different groups of customers.
examples.zh: 这个「教学案例」讲了一家试图服务两类顾客的自行车店。

examples.en: Our tutor shortened the teaching case so everyone could read it before the afternoon seminar.
examples.zh: 导师缩短了「教学案例」，让大家在下午研讨课前都能读完。

words.enDefinition: a teaching case that asks learners to recommend a choice facing a person or organisation

examples.en: The decision case ended before the manager chose whether to open a second repair booth.
examples.zh: 「决策型案例」在经理决定是否开第二个维修摊位之前结束。

examples.en: In the decision case, we had to choose between relocating the shop and staying near campus.
examples.zh: 在这个「决策型案例」中，我们得在搬店和留在校园附近之间作选择。

words.enDefinition: the central person in a case, often the manager whose decision students are asked to consider

examples.en: The case protagonist had only a week to decide what to do with the spare room.
examples.zh: 「案例主角」只有一周时间决定怎么使用空置房间。

examples.en: We tried to see the dispute from the perspective of the case protagonist before voting.
examples.zh: 投票前，我们试着从「案例主角」的角度看待这场争执。

words.enDefinition: a person or group with authority to choose what action to take

examples.en: The brief said the decision maker was the founder, even though the manager had prepared the figures.
examples.zh: 简报写明「决策者」是创始人，尽管数据是经理准备的。

examples.en: Our group asked whether the decision maker could change the opening hours without consulting the board.
examples.zh: 我们小组问，「决策者」能不能在不征求董事会意见的情况下调整营业时间。

words.enDefinition: a situation requiring a choice between options with substantial or conflicting drawbacks

examples.en: The decision dilemma was whether to lower prices or keep enough income to staff the counter.
examples.zh: 团队面临的「决策两难」是降价，还是保住给柜台配备员工所需的收入。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to explain the decision dilemma before suggesting an answer to the case.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先说明「决策两难」体现在哪里，再为案例提出解决办法。

words.enDefinition: a moment or stage when someone must choose which action to take next

examples.en: The case reached a decision point when the landlord offered a different unit for the workshop.
examples.zh: 房东为工作室提供另一个铺位时，案例到了「决策时点」。

examples.en: We stopped reading at the decision point and wrote down our preferred course of action.
examples.zh: 我们读到「决策时点」就停下来，记下了自己倾向的做法。

words.enDefinition: the order in which events in a case took place

examples.en: I drew a case chronology because the manager's notes discussed earlier events out of order.
examples.zh: 经理的记录没按时间顺序讲早先的事件，我画了「案例事件时间线」。

examples.en: The case chronology showed that the shop changed its hours before the complaints began.
examples.zh: 「案例事件时间线」显示，店铺调整营业时间在先，顾客开始投诉在后。

words.enDefinition: the main account in a case that presents its context, events and participants

examples.en: The case narrative described the first month of trading from the owner's point of view.
examples.zh: 「案例叙述」从店主视角讲了开始营业的第一个月。

examples.en: We checked the case narrative to see who knew about the delivery problem that week.
examples.zh: 我们查看「案例叙述」，确认当周哪些人知道送货问题。

collocations: refer back to the case narrative

words.enDefinition: information stated or established in a case that learners can use in their analysis

examples.en: I separated the case facts from my guesses about why the staff had left early.
examples.zh: 我把「案例给出的事实」和自己对员工为什么提前离开的猜测分开了。

examples.en: The professor asked which case facts supported keeping the service open on weekday evenings.
examples.zh: 教授问，有哪些「案例给出的事实」支持工作日晚间继续提供服务。

collocations: base an argument on the case facts

words.enDefinition: a set of readings and evidence distributed for a class, case competition or case exercise

examples.en: The case packet included a description of the shop and two tables of monthly orders.
examples.zh: 「案例材料包」包含店铺介绍和两张月度订单表。

examples.en: We downloaded the case packet before meeting to decide who would analyse the customer figures.
examples.zh: 我们先下载了「案例材料包」，再开会决定谁分析顾客数据。

words.enDefinition: an item attached to a case, such as a chart, table or sample document

examples.en: A case exhibit showed how repair demand changed between term time and the summer break.
examples.zh: 一份「案例附录材料」展示了学期内和暑假期间维修需求的变化。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to refer to a case exhibit when discussing the owner's options.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们在讨论店主的选择时参考一份「案例附录材料」。

words.enDefinition: a note explaining details, definitions or limitations in a chart or other exhibit

examples.en: The exhibit note explained that the table counted bookings rather than completed repair jobs.
examples.zh: 「附表或附图的注释」说明，表里统计的是预约数量，只凭这张表看不出修了多少件。

examples.en: I checked the exhibit note before comparing sales figures from the two different locations.
examples.zh: 比较两个地点的销售额之前，我读了「附表或附图的注释」。

words.enDefinition: notes made before a class about a case's facts, uncertainties and possible decisions

examples.en: My pre-class case notes included two questions about the shop's supply costs in winter.
examples.zh: 我的「课前案例笔记」里有两个关于那家店冬季供货成本的问题。

examples.en: We compared pre-class case notes over lunch before joining the rest of the tutorial group.
examples.zh: 加入其他辅导课同学前，我们午饭时对比了彼此的「课前案例笔记」。

words.enDefinition: work done before discussing a case, including reading it and developing an initial analysis

examples.en: The tutor allocated forty minutes for case preparation so we could check all three tables.
examples.zh: 导师留了四十分钟做「案例课前准备」，让我们有时间核对三张表。

examples.en: Good case preparation helped me contribute an example before the discussion moved to the figures.
examples.zh: 做好「案例课前准备」后，我能在讨论转到数据之前举出一个例子。

words.enDefinition: to add notes, questions or comments directly to the case material while reading

examples.en: I used two colours to annotate the case and mark what the manager did not know.
examples.zh: 我用两种颜色「给案例材料加批注」，标出经理当时还不知道的事。

examples.en: We were asked to annotate the case before comparing recommendations with our small discussion groups.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们先「给案例材料加批注」，然后再在讨论小组里比较建议。

collocations: annotate the case as you read
use comments to annotate the case
ask students to annotate the case

words.enDefinition: the work of examining a case and reaching a reasoned view independently of other participants

examples.en: My independent case analysis helped me see two plausible ways to use the spare room.
examples.zh: 通过「独立案例分析」，我看到了空房间的两种可行用途。

examples.en: I began my independent case analysis before anyone shared their views in the small group.
examples.zh: 小组里还没人说自己的看法前，我就开始了「独立案例分析」。

words.enDefinition: a conversation in a small group to compare case interpretations or possible decisions

examples.en: During the small-group case discussion, we found that our two recommendations used the same evidence.
examples.zh: 「小组案例讨论」中，我们发现两份不同的建议用了同样的证据。

examples.en: The small-group case discussion ended with one question that we took to the whole class.
examples.zh: 「小组案例讨论」结束时，我们留了一个问题交给全班讨论。

collocations: prepare for a small-group case discussion

words.enDefinition: a short report or presentation summarising the situation and main issues of a case

examples.en: The case briefing opened with the choice the cafe owner needed to make before winter.
examples.zh: 「案例简报」一开头就介绍了咖啡馆老板入冬前要作的选择。

examples.en: I used our case briefing to explain what figures the class would see on the next slide.
examples.zh: 我用「案例简报」说明大家会在下一页幻灯片看到哪些数据。

words.enDefinition: a participant who makes the initial statement in a case discussion before the discussion moves to others

examples.en: As the case opener, I explained which option I would choose if I ran the shop.
examples.zh: 作为「案例讨论开场发言者」，我说明了如果自己开这家店会选哪个方案。

examples.en: The tutor asked a different student to be the case opener for each weekly class.
examples.zh: 每周上课时，导师都会请不同的学生担任「案例讨论开场发言者」。

collocations: prepare to be the case opener

words.enDefinition: guiding a case discussion so learners examine evidence, exchange perspectives and reach conclusions

examples.en: We practised case facilitation by taking turns asking quiet group members to share their reasoning.
examples.zh: 我们轮流请比较安静的组员分享理由，以练习「案例讨论引导」。

examples.en: The instructor gave us feedback on case facilitation after we tried leading the evening session.
examples.zh: 我们试着主导晚上的讨论后，导师给了我们关于「案例讨论引导」的反馈。

words.enDefinition: a teacher's plan for organising notes and ideas on a board during a lesson

examples.en: The instructor's board plan reserved space for each option and the evidence that supported it.
examples.zh: 导师的「课堂板书规划」给每个方案及其支撑证据都留了位置。

examples.en: I prepared a board plan before leading a short discussion on the case's final decision.
examples.zh: 主持关于案例最终决定的短讨论前，我做了「课堂板书规划」。

words.enDefinition: a final summary that connects the main ideas, findings or viewpoints in a lesson

examples.en: The tutor's end-of-class synthesis connected our pricing debate to the shop's limited working hours.
examples.zh: 导师的「课堂结尾综合归纳」把我们对定价的讨论与店铺营业时间有限联系起来。

examples.en: I wrote down the end-of-class synthesis because it helped me understand why the recommendations differed.
examples.zh: 我记下了「课堂结尾的综合归纳」，因为它帮我理解了各项建议为何不同。

collocations: take notes on an end-of-class synthesis

words.enDefinition: a discussion after analysing or presenting a case to reflect on decisions, reasoning and lessons

examples.en: Our case debrief focused on which facts we had missed in the first round of reading.
examples.zh: 我们的「案例讨论复盘」着重看第一遍阅读时漏掉了哪些事实。

examples.en: The case debrief helped us see why both options had looked reasonable at first.
examples.zh: 「案例讨论复盘」让我们看明白，为什么两种方案起初都显得合理。

collocations: take part in a case debrief

words.enDefinition: a guide for instructors on how to teach a case, often with questions and possible analysis

examples.en: The course team used a teaching note to organise discussion around the moment of decision.
examples.zh: 课程团队依据「教学指导说明」，围绕需要决策的时刻组织讨论。

examples.en: I helped my supervisor review a teaching note for a new business school case.
examples.zh: 我协助导师审阅了一份商学院新案例的「教学指导说明」。

words.enDefinition: a case designed to be taught alongside another case to give a contrasting or additional perspective

examples.en: The companion case presented the same shop's move from the staff members' point of view.
examples.zh: 「配套案例」从员工视角讲述了同一家店搬迁的事情。

examples.en: We studied the companion case after discussing the original one from the perspective of customers.
examples.zh: 我们从顾客角度讨论了原案例，随后学习了「配套案例」。

collocations: teach a companion case alongside the original

words.enDefinition: a short account explaining what happened after the events or decision described in a case

examples.en: The case epilogue revealed how the manager's decision affected the repair business during the next year.
examples.zh: 「案例后记」讲了经理的决定怎样影响维修店下一年的经营。

examples.en: We read the case epilogue only after presenting our own recommendations in the seminar.
examples.zh: 我们在研讨课上陈述了自己的建议，之后才读「案例后记」。

words.expression: put yourself in the manager's shoes
words.lemma: put yourself in the manager's shoes
words.enDefinition: to imagine the manager's situation, responsibilities and available information when judging a decision
acceptedEnVariants: put yourself in the manager's shoes

examples.en: Try to put yourself in the manager's shoes before judging her decision to cut evening hours.
examples.zh: 评判她缩减晚间营业时间的决定前，试着「站在经理的立场考虑」。

examples.en: Our lecturer said to put yourself in the manager's shoes when comparing the two proposed budgets.
examples.zh: 讲师说，对比两份预算方案时要「站在经理的立场考虑」。

collocations: try to put yourself in the manager's shoes
ask students to put themselves in the manager's shoes
put yourself in the manager's shoes for a moment

words.enDefinition: a choice made when relevant conditions or possible outcomes are not fully known

examples.en: The case illustrated a decision under uncertainty because no one could predict demand after the holiday.
examples.zh: 这是个「不确定条件下的决策」案例，因为没人能预测假期后的需求。

examples.en: We modelled the decision under uncertainty using two plausible levels of customer demand for the next term.
examples.zh: 我们采用下学期两种可能的需求水平，模拟了「不确定条件下的决策」。

words.enDefinition: the latest time by which a choice must be made

examples.en: The decision deadline was Friday because the owner had to reply to the landlord that afternoon.
examples.zh: 「决策截止时间」是周五，因为店主得在当天下午给房东答复。

examples.en: We moved the decision deadline after the supplier agreed to hold the quote for another week.
examples.zh: 供应商同意把报价再保留一周，我们相应调整了「决策截止时间」。

words.enDefinition: a difficult problem that requires someone in a management role to set priorities or take action

examples.en: The managerial challenge was how to keep both services running with only one experienced worker.
examples.zh: 「管理难题」在于，只有一名有经验的员工，如何同时维持两项服务。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which managerial challenge had the greatest effect on the business that year.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪项「管理难题」对那年企业的影响最大。

words.enDefinition: the result a decision is intended to achieve

examples.en: Our main decision objective was to reduce the waiting time without increasing the team's weekly costs.
examples.zh: 我们主要的「决策目标」是在不增加团队每周成本的情况下缩短等待时间。

examples.en: The group changed its decision objective after learning that the shop already had enough customers.
examples.zh: 得知店铺已有足够多的顾客后，小组更改了「决策目标」。

words.enDefinition: a choice that can realistically be carried out with the available resources and time

examples.en: When the room closed earlier than expected, our only feasible option was to meet at noon.
examples.zh: 房间提前关闭后，我们唯一的「可行选项」是中午开会。

examples.en: The professor asked us to provide a feasible option within the shop's staffing and budget limits.
examples.zh: 教授请我们在店铺的人手与预算限制内提供一个「可行选项」。

words.enDefinition: a restriction that limits what a business can realistically decide or do

examples.en: Lack of space became a business constraint once the store started accepting more repair orders.
examples.zh: 店铺开始接更多维修订单后，空间不足成了「业务约束条件」。

examples.en: We treated the long delivery window as a business constraint when assessing the proposed schedule.
examples.zh: 评估拟议日程时，我们把送货时间范围太宽视为「业务约束条件」。

words.enDefinition: a constraint that holds with equality at a given feasible solution, using an allowance or meeting a required minimum exactly

examples.en: The case asked whether storage space or staffing hours formed the binding constraint for weekly repairs.
examples.zh: 案例问，对于每周维修量，「紧约束」是存储空间还是员工工时。

examples.en: The staffing limit was a binding constraint because our best plan used every available hour.
examples.zh: 最优方案恰好用完了所有可用工时，所以工时上限是「紧约束」。

words.enDefinition: a limit caused by relevant information being unavailable, incomplete or difficult to obtain in time

examples.en: The information constraint meant the team could compare only the prices it had already received.
examples.zh: 受「信息受限条件」影响，团队只能比较已经收到的报价。

examples.en: We discussed the information constraint before recommending that the owner delay signing the agreement until Friday.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「信息受限条件」，然后建议店主把签约推迟到周五。

words.enDefinition: a choice in which using limited resources for one need leaves less for another

examples.en: The resource trade-off was between spending the weekend on training and extending the stall's hours.
examples.zh: 「资源分配取舍」在于用周末做培训，还是延长摊位的营业时间。

examples.en: We explained the resource trade-off when comparing two different ways to strengthen the collection service.
examples.zh: 比较两种改进取货服务的做法时，我们解释了其中的「资源分配取舍」。

words.enDefinition: goals that are difficult to achieve together because improving one may mean sacrificing another

examples.en: The club had competing objectives because it wanted to reduce prices and extend opening hours.
examples.zh: 社团想降价，也想延长营业时间，面临「相互冲突的目标」。

examples.en: The class listed competing objectives before deciding how the business should respond to longer queues.
examples.zh: 全班先列了「相互冲突的目标」，再判断商家该怎样应对队伍变长。

words.enDefinition: the needs, priorities or concerns of people affected by a decision or project

examples.en: We compared stakeholder interests after reading how the relocation would affect staff, students and suppliers.
examples.zh: 我们了解搬迁对员工、学生和供应商的影响后，比较了「各利益相关方的诉求」。

examples.en: The professor asked which stakeholder interests had received too little attention in the first proposal.
examples.zh: 教授问，首份方案对哪些「利益相关方的诉求」考虑得不够。

words.enDefinition: a constraint that is not reached exactly at the given feasible solution and has some unused allowance

examples.en: The budget was a nonbinding constraint because our chosen plan cost less than the limit.
examples.zh: 我们选的方案花费低于上限，因此预算是「非紧约束」。

examples.en: I marked the available desks as a nonbinding constraint because several were left unused.
examples.zh: 还有几张桌子没用，我将可用桌数标为「非紧约束」。

collocations: a nonbinding constraint at the solution
show why a constraint is nonbinding

words.enDefinition: the factors or standards used to judge and compare possible choices

examples.en: Our decision criteria included setup cost, staff time and how easily students could reach the stall.
examples.zh: 我们的「决策标准」包括布置成本、工时和学生到摊位的便利程度。

examples.en: The group agreed on decision criteria before reading any of the detailed proposals from suppliers.
examples.zh: 小组在阅读供应商的详细方案之前先商定了「决策标准」。

words.enDefinition: evaluation criteria to which weights have been assigned to reflect their relative importance

examples.en: We used weighted criteria so that location counted more than the colour of the fixtures.
examples.zh: 我们采用「带权重的评估标准」，让地段比固定装置的颜色占更大比重。

examples.en: The team adjusted the weighted criteria after learning how important afternoon access was to customers.
examples.zh: 团队得知下午能进店对顾客很重要，调整了「带权重的评估标准」。

words.enDefinition: a value expressing how much one criterion counts in a comparison with other criteria

examples.en: We adjusted the criterion weight for price once the group realised most options were affordable.
examples.zh: 小组发现大多数方案都负担得起，便调整了价格这项「评估标准的权重」。

examples.en: The spreadsheet showed how each criterion weight affected the total score for the room.
examples.zh: 表格显示，各项「评估标准的权重」怎样影响该房间的总分。

words.enDefinition: a table that records how each option rates against each criterion, with weights when needed

examples.en: Our decision matrix compared three venues by cost, equipment, location and available opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们用「决策矩阵」比较三个场地的成本、设备、地点和可开放时段。

examples.en: The decision matrix made it clear why the cheapest room had not scored highest.
examples.zh: 「决策矩阵」说明了为什么最便宜的房间得分并非最高。

words.enDefinition: a branching diagram showing choices, uncertain events and possible outcomes

examples.en: We drew a decision tree to compare what could happen if the club ordered early.
examples.zh: 我们画了「决策树」，比较社团提前下单后可能出现的不同结果。

examples.en: The decision tree showed two possible outcomes after the manager chose the larger space.
examples.zh: 「决策树」标出了经理选择较大场地后可能出现的两种结果。

words.enDefinition: a point in a decision tree where a decision maker chooses among actions

examples.en: We marked the decision node where the owner could renew the lease or move elsewhere.
examples.zh: 我们标出了「决策节点」，店主要在这里选择续租还是搬去别处。

examples.en: Before adding the costs, I checked whether we had labelled the correct decision node.
examples.zh: 加上成本之前，我核对了有没有把正确的「决策节点」标出来。

words.enDefinition: a point in a decision tree representing an uncertain event, with branches for possible outcomes

examples.en: The chance node showed two possibilities for demand during the first school holiday of the year.
examples.zh: 「随机事件节点」列出了本年度第一次学校放假时需求可能有的两种情况。

examples.en: We added a chance node after choosing the larger room because attendance was still unknown.
examples.zh: 选择较大的房间后，出席人数还不确定，我们因此加了一个「随机事件节点」。

collocations: assign probabilities at a chance node

words.enDefinition: the probability of a particular outcome given that its chance node has been reached

examples.en: We changed one branch probability after finding better records for the previous month's sales.
examples.zh: 找到上个月更完整的销售记录后，我们调整了一项「分支概率」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain the branch probability for lower demand during the summer.
examples.zh: 导师请我们说明夏季需求下降这一项的「分支概率」从何而来。

words.enDefinition: a result that follows a decision, sometimes depending on events outside the decision maker's control

examples.en: We could not know the decision outcome until students tried the new pickup hours.
examples.zh: 要等学生试过新的自取时段，我们才知道「决策结果」。

examples.en: The case compared each possible decision outcome with what the manager had originally hoped to achieve.
examples.zh: 案例把每一种可能的「决策结果」与经理原先希望达到的结果作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the endpoint of a path through a decision tree, showing the resulting outcome or payoff

examples.en: We wrote the final profit beside each terminal node at the end of the tree.
examples.zh: 我们在决策树末端的每个「终端节点」旁写了最终利润。

examples.en: Each branch led to a different terminal node because the repair costs were different.
examples.zh: 各条分支通向不同的「终端节点」，因为维修成本不同。

collocations: calculate the value at a terminal node

words.enDefinition: a written account of how the conditions and assumptions in a scenario fit together

examples.en: Our scenario narrative explained why orders would increase shortly before the campus festival began.
examples.zh: 我们的「情景文字描述」解释了为什么校园节庆开始前不久订单会增加。

examples.en: The tutor asked for a scenario narrative alongside the table of estimated visitor numbers.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在预估访客人数的表格旁附上「情景文字描述」。

collocations: support assumptions with a scenario narrative

words.enDefinition: the most favourable plausible set of events or conditions considered in a plan

examples.en: In the best-case scenario, both printers would work and the room would open on time.
examples.zh: 在「最理想的情景」下，两台打印机都能用，房间也会准时开放。

examples.en: We put an estimate for the best-case scenario beside the figure we actually expected.
examples.zh: 我们把「最理想的情景」的估计值列在实际预期的数字旁。

words.enDefinition: the least favourable plausible set of events or conditions considered in a plan

examples.en: The worst-case scenario combined a late delivery with the loss of our second collection desk.
examples.zh: 「最坏的情景」是送货延迟，同时失去第二处自取台。

examples.en: We discussed the worst-case scenario before deciding how much spare time to put in the schedule.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论了「最坏的情景」，再决定在日程里预留多少时间。

words.enDefinition: an examination of several possible situations to see how their results differ

examples.en: Our scenario comparison showed that the same choice worked whether demand increased slowly or quickly.
examples.zh: 「情景对比」表明，无论需求增长快还是慢，同一选择都能行得通。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to add a scenario comparison to our slides before recommending any option.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在推荐方案前，把「情景对比」放进幻灯片。

words.enDefinition: an assumption about how an activity will run, such as hours, capacity or staff availability

examples.en: One operating assumption was that two people could pack all the orders before the store closed.
examples.zh: 一项「运营假设」是，两个人能在关店前打包完所有订单。

examples.en: The owner challenged our operating assumption about how long the counter would stay open on Fridays.
examples.zh: 店主质疑了我们关于周五柜台营业时长的「运营假设」。

words.enDefinition: to question whether a belief used in an analysis is justified by the available evidence

examples.en: I decided to challenge an assumption about costs after finding the original quotation in the appendix.
examples.zh: 在附录里找到原始报价后，我决定「质疑一项关于成本的假设」。

examples.en: The case discussion gave us a chance to challenge an assumption shared by all three groups.
examples.zh: 案例讨论让我们有机会「质疑一项假设」，三个小组都默认它成立。

collocations: be willing to challenge an assumption

words.enDefinition: something that makes the value, timing or outcome of another thing difficult to predict

examples.en: The date of the equipment delivery was our biggest source of uncertainty for the weekend market.
examples.zh: 器材送到的日期，是我们办周末集市时最大的一项「不确定性的来源」。

examples.en: We identified another source of uncertainty when the landlord declined to confirm the rent in advance.
examples.zh: 房东不肯提前确认租金时，我们找到了另一项「不确定性的来源」。

words.enDefinition: a difference between information currently available and information needed to understand or decide something

examples.en: Our biggest information gap was who could approve a trial of the later pickup hours.
examples.zh: 我们最大的「信息缺口」是，不知道谁有权批准试行晚一点的取货时段。

examples.en: The professor asked how we would close the information gap before the manager had to decide.
examples.zh: 教授问，我们会怎样在经理必须作出决定前填补「信息缺口」。

words.enDefinition: a weakness in available data that affects what conclusions can reasonably be drawn

examples.en: One data limitation was that the report combined returns from both stores into one total.
examples.zh: 一项「数据局限」是报告把两家门店的退货量合成一个总数。

examples.en: We noted the data limitation beside our estimate so readers could see what was uncertain.
examples.zh: 我们在估计值旁注明了「数据局限」，让读者知道哪里有不确定性。

words.enDefinition: evidence from different sources suggesting conclusions that do not agree with each other

examples.en: We found conflicting evidence about whether bookings fell after the change in collection time.
examples.zh: 关于自取时间更改后预约量是否下降，我们找到了「相互矛盾的证据」。

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to explain conflicting evidence before arguing for a change in hours.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们在主张调整营业时间前，先解释「相互矛盾的证据」。

words.enDefinition: a comparison that suggests an inaccurate conclusion because important differences are ignored or hidden

examples.en: Comparing total visits gave a misleading comparison because one shop was open twice as long.
examples.zh: 比较到访总量是「会引起误解的比较」，因为其中一家店开门时间是另一家的两倍。

examples.en: The lecturer asked us to correct a misleading comparison in the first table of our report.
examples.zh: 讲师请我们改正报告第一张表里一处「会引起误解的比较」。

words.enDefinition: an approximate figure calculated from incomplete information or without a detailed method

examples.en: We made a rough estimate of the storage area needed before surveying the whole building.
examples.zh: 勘察整栋楼之前，我们对需要多大储存区做了「粗略估算」。

examples.en: The rough estimate helped us decide whether the larger venue was worth examining in more detail.
examples.zh: 「粗略估算」帮我们判断，值不值得再仔细看看那个较大的场地。

words.enDefinition: a quick approximate calculation used to check the scale or feasibility of something

examples.en: A back-of-the-envelope calculation suggested we could serve forty people before the room closed that evening.
examples.zh: 「快速粗算」表明，当晚房间关闭前我们能服务四十个人。

examples.en: I did a back-of-the-envelope calculation to check whether the stock would last through the weekend.
examples.zh: 我做了次「快速粗算」，确认库存够不够用到周末结束。

words.enDefinition: an estimate aimed at finding the approximate scale, such as tens, hundreds or thousands

examples.en: We needed an order-of-magnitude estimate of how many shelves a campus-wide service might use.
examples.zh: 我们需要对覆盖全校的服务所需货架数做一个「数量级估算」。

examples.en: An order-of-magnitude estimate was enough to show that one small room could not hold the stock.
examples.zh: 做个「数量级估算」就足以看出，一间小屋装不下这些库存。

words.enDefinition: an assumption introduced to make an analysis manageable by leaving out some complexity

examples.en: For our first estimate, we made a simplifying assumption that each booking took the same time.
examples.zh: 第一次估算时，我们作了个「简化假设」，设定每笔预约处理用时相同。

examples.en: I stated the simplifying assumption beneath the chart so readers could judge its effect.
examples.zh: 我在图下写明了「简化假设」，让读者判断它的影响。

words.enDefinition: a quick check that a result makes sense in relation to what is already known

examples.en: I did a reasonableness check by comparing the total with actual sales from last year.
examples.zh: 我把总数与去年实际销售数据比较，做了「合理性检查」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a reasonableness check before we cited the figure in our recommendation.
examples.zh: 导师要求我们在建议里引用该数字前做一次「合理性检查」。

words.zhGloss: 对假设变化的敏感程度
words.enDefinition: how much a result changes when a particular assumption changes
acceptedZhAnswers: 对假设变化的敏感程度

examples.en: We tested sensitivity to an assumption about opening hours by trying three different closing times.
examples.zh: 我们代入三种关门时间，检验结果「对营业时间假设变化的敏感程度」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which estimate had the greatest sensitivity to an assumption about delivery times.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪个估计值「对送货时间假设变化最敏感」。

words.enDefinition: a level or condition at which the preferred choice or recommended action changes

examples.en: The team chose a decision threshold of fifty bookings before paying for the larger room.
examples.zh: 团队把五十笔预约设为「决策阈值」，达到后才付费租用较大的房间。

examples.en: We compared the forecast with our decision threshold before recommending whether to keep the evening service.
examples.zh: 在建议是否保留晚间服务前，我们把预测值和「决策阈值」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: an estimate intended to show the high end of what a quantity could plausibly be

examples.en: Our upper-bound estimate assumed that every participating society would request the largest equipment kit.
examples.zh: 我们的「上界估计」假设，每个参与社团都会申请最大的设备套件。

examples.en: We used the upper-bound estimate to see whether even the largest storeroom would be adequate.
examples.zh: 我们通过「上界估计」检查，即使最大的储藏室是否也够用。

words.enDefinition: an estimate intended to show the low end of what a quantity could plausibly be

examples.en: Our lower-bound estimate included only bookings that had already been confirmed by each group.
examples.zh: 「下界估计」只纳入各小组已经确认的预约。

examples.en: The lower-bound estimate suggested we still needed two workers even if no walk-ins arrived.
examples.zh: 「下界估计」表明，即使没有现场来访者，也需要两名员工。

words.enDefinition: to remove an option from consideration because it fails a basic requirement

examples.en: We used the budget limit to screen out an alternative that required a second lease.
examples.zh: 我们用预算限制「筛掉一个备选方案」，因为它还需要第二份租约。

examples.en: A short preliminary check helped us screen out an alternative before spending time on calculations.
examples.zh: 短暂的初步核查让我们在花时间计算前「筛掉一个备选方案」。

collocations: use criteria to screen out an alternative
decide to screen out an alternative

words.enDefinition: to examine how different options are expected to turn out before choosing one

examples.en: We met after class to compare projected outcomes for two possible collection locations on campus.
examples.zh: 我们课后碰头，「比较校园两处自取地点的预测结果」。

examples.en: Our slides compare projected outcomes using the same demand and cost assumptions for both options.
examples.zh: 我们的幻灯片为两个方案采用相同的需求和成本假设，「比较预测结果」。

collocations: compare projected outcomes side by side
use a chart to compare projected outcomes
compare projected outcomes under different assumptions

words.enDefinition: to check whether the action recommended would still make sense or work under relevant conditions

examples.en: We decided to test the recommendation against records from a busier week before submitting it.
examples.zh: 我们决定在提交前依据一周较忙时的记录「检验建议方案」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to test the recommendation assuming the owner could hire only one person.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在店主只能雇一人的条件下「检验建议方案」。

collocations: test the recommendation under different conditions
find a way to test the recommendation

words.enDefinition: to explain why a recommended choice is sound when others question it

examples.en: I had to defend a recommendation the team made despite some uncertainty about customer demand.
examples.zh: 尽管顾客需求还不确定，我得「为团队的建议说明理由」。

examples.en: The judges asked our group to defend a recommendation using the figures in the case packet.
examples.zh: 评审请我们小组用案例材料包里的数据「为这项建议说明理由」。

collocations: be prepared to defend a recommendation
use evidence to defend a recommendation

words.enDefinition: to advise which step or series of steps a person or organisation should take

examples.en: The assignment asked us to recommend a course of action before the store's lease expired.
examples.zh: 作业要求我们在店铺租约到期之前「建议一套行动方案」。

examples.en: We had to recommend a course of action even though the demand forecast was incomplete.
examples.zh: 虽然需求预测并不完整，我们还是得「建议一套行动方案」。

collocations: recommend a course of action to management
ask someone to recommend a course of action
use the evidence to recommend a course of action

words.enDefinition: a recommendation grounded in relevant evidence rather than opinion alone

examples.en: Our tutor wanted an evidence-based recommendation that addressed the shortage of staff during the evening.
examples.zh: 导师希望给出一项「有证据支持的建议」，解决晚间人手不足的问题。

examples.en: We wrote an evidence-based recommendation after comparing seasonal sales and speaking to workers at both locations.
examples.zh: 我们比较了季节销售情况，还与两处员工交谈，之后写了一项「有证据支持的建议」。

words.enDefinition: a short document that proposes a decision and explains the reasons and expected effects

examples.en: The recommendation memo asked the owner to test evening pickup before moving the whole store.
examples.zh: 「建议备忘录」请店主先试行晚间自取，再考虑全店搬迁。

examples.en: I rewrote our recommendation memo to put the suggested action before the detailed calculations.
examples.zh: 我重写了「建议备忘录」，把建议采取的行动放在详细计算之前。

words.enDefinition: a concise document recording a decision, its rationale and relevant next steps

examples.en: The manager circulated a decision memo after choosing to keep the current collection point.
examples.zh: 经理决定保留现有自取点后，传阅了一份「决策备忘录」。

examples.en: Our decision memo explained why the business had selected a smaller space near the library.
examples.zh: 我们的「决策备忘录」说明了企业为什么选图书馆附近较小的场地。

collocations: record a choice in a decision memo

words.enDefinition: the reasoning that explains why a particular choice was made

examples.en: The decision rationale explained why student access mattered more than the lowest possible rent.
examples.zh: 「决策理由」说明了为什么方便学生到达比把租金压到最低更重要。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the decision rationale still held if the evening classes moved online.
examples.zh: 讲师问，如果晚课改到线上，「决策理由」是否依然成立。

words.enDefinition: the order in which the steps required to put a plan into effect take place

examples.en: Our implementation sequence put staff training before any announcement about the new collection hours.
examples.zh: 我们的「实施顺序」把员工培训排在发布新的自取时间通知之前。

examples.en: The group revised the implementation sequence after learning that the shelves would arrive next month.
examples.zh: 小组得知货架要下个月到，修改了「实施顺序」。

words.enDefinition: a possible problem that could hinder a plan while it is being put into effect

examples.en: One implementation risk was that staff would not have time to learn the new booking process.
examples.zh: 一项「实施风险」是员工可能没时间学习新的预约流程。

examples.en: The manager asked us to identify an implementation risk that the schedule could help reduce.
examples.zh: 经理请我们找出可通过调整时间安排来降低的一项「实施风险」。

words.enDefinition: a condition that must be met before a plan can be put into action

examples.en: A second collection table was a prerequisite for implementation of the new pickup process.
examples.zh: 设第二张自取桌是启用新取货流程的「实施前提」。

examples.en: The case identified staff training as a prerequisite for implementation before the shop advertised longer hours.
examples.zh: 案例把员工培训列为店铺宣传延长营业时间的「实施前提」。

collocations: state the main prerequisite for implementation

words.enDefinition: how realistic it is to carry out a proposal under actual conditions

examples.en: We checked practical feasibility by asking who could staff the repair desk at seven.
examples.zh: 我们问了谁能七点去维修台值班，以验证「实际可行性」。

examples.en: The tutor wanted us to discuss practical feasibility as well as the strength of the idea.
examples.zh: 导师希望我们除了说创意的优点，也讨论「实际可行性」。

words.enDefinition: the first action to take now that a decision or event has occurred

examples.en: Our immediate next step was to ask the library whether it could provide another table.
examples.zh: 我们「眼下的下一步」是问图书馆能不能再提供一张桌子。

examples.en: The case presenter ended by explaining the immediate next step before discussing longer plans.
examples.zh: 案例演讲人在结尾先说明「眼下的下一步」，再谈长远计划。

collocations: agree on the immediate next step

words.enDefinition: the money or other benefits lost or spent because action is taken later

examples.en: We weighed the cost of delay against the possibility of receiving better information next week.
examples.zh: 我们在「延迟造成的成本」与下周可能拿到更好信息之间作权衡。

examples.en: The cost of delay rose once the repair desk started turning people away each afternoon.
examples.zh: 维修台开始每天下午都不得不谢绝一些人后，「延迟造成的成本」上升了。

collocations: compare the cost of delay with the benefits

words.enDefinition: an action intended to reduce the chance or severity of a potential problem

examples.en: As a risk mitigation step, we booked a spare room in case the library closed.
examples.zh: 作为一项「降低风险的措施」，我们订了间备用房间，以防图书馆关闭。

examples.en: The adviser asked which risk mitigation step would help if the evening volunteer became unavailable.
examples.zh: 顾问问，如果晚间志愿者来不了，哪一项「降低风险的措施」能帮上忙。

words.enDefinition: an event, result or condition that prompts a planned decision or arrangement to be reviewed

examples.en: A fall in bookings for two weeks was our review trigger for the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 预约量若连续两周下降，就满足重新评估新营业时间的「触发复核的条件」。

examples.en: The group chose a review trigger so managers would know when to look at the decision again.
examples.zh: 小组选了一个「触发复核的条件」，让经理知道什么时候要重新审视这项决定。

words.enDefinition: the choice put forward as best suited to the situation after considering the alternatives

examples.en: The recommended option kept the shop near campus while moving only the collection point.
examples.zh: 「推荐方案」让店铺留在校园附近，只搬自取点。

examples.en: We tested whether the recommended option still made sense when the delivery cost increased.
examples.zh: 我们检验了当送货成本上升时，「推荐方案」是否依旧合理。

collocations: compare the recommended option with alternatives

words.enDefinition: risk that remains after actions have been taken to reduce it

examples.en: The residual risk was that a visitor might still walk into the old collection room.
examples.zh: 「剩余风险」是有人仍可能走进旧自取室。

examples.en: Our report described the residual risk even after signs had been placed at both entrances.
examples.zh: 即使两个入口都放了指示牌，报告仍说明了「剩余风险」。

words.enDefinition: advice that applies only if a stated condition or event holds

examples.en: We wrote a contingent recommendation that depended on the landlord approving a second storage room.
examples.zh: 我们写了项「取决于条件的建议」，前提是房东同意再开放一间储物室。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain when the contingent recommendation should actually be put into effect.
examples.zh: 导师请我们解释「取决于条件的建议」应在什么情况下真正实施。

words.enDefinition: a recommendation for what to do if the preferred choice becomes impossible or unsuitable

examples.en: Our fallback recommendation was to share the existing counter instead of renting the larger space.
examples.zh: 「备用建议」是共用现有柜台，不租那个更大的场地。

examples.en: I added a fallback recommendation because the store had not yet secured funding for repairs.
examples.zh: 店铺的维修经费还没落实，所以我补了一项「备用建议」。

words.enDefinition: to consider a previous choice again in light of more information or changed conditions

examples.en: We agreed to revisit the decision after students had used the new counter for a month.
examples.zh: 我们同意，让学生使用新柜台一个月后，再「重新审视决定」。

examples.en: The manager had to revisit the decision when the printer failed again during the fair.
examples.zh: 打印机在展会期间再次出故障，经理不得不「重新审视决定」。

collocations: have reason to revisit the decision

words.enDefinition: a choice that can be changed or undone later without disproportionate cost or harm

examples.en: Changing the collection sign was a reversible decision, so we tried the new wording first.
examples.zh: 换自取标牌是「可撤回的决定」，所以我们先试了新版文字。

examples.en: We preferred a reversible decision while we still had little evidence about evening demand.
examples.zh: 晚间需求的证据还很少，我们更愿意作「可撤回的决定」。

words.enDefinition: a choice that cannot be undone or can be undone only with great difficulty

examples.en: Selling the second repair bench was an irreversible decision for our small team that term.
examples.zh: 当学期对我们这个小团队来说，卖掉第二张维修台是「难以撤回的决定」。

examples.en: The tutor asked what evidence we would need before making an irreversible decision about the shop.
examples.zh: 导师问，在对店铺作出「难以撤回的决定」前，我们需要哪些证据。

words.enDefinition: a planned point at which progress and evidence are reviewed before a later decision is taken

examples.en: We scheduled a decision checkpoint after the first ten orders in the autumn trial.
examples.zh: 我们把秋季试点完成头十笔订单的时点设为「决策检查点」。

examples.en: The next decision checkpoint gave us time to compare feedback from both collection locations.
examples.zh: 下一次「决策检查点」让我们有时间比较两处自取点的反馈。

words.enDefinition: an assessment after a decision that examines its implementation, results or quality of reasoning

examples.en: The post-decision review found that more students used the later pickup time than we had expected.
examples.zh: 「决策后复盘」发现，晚一点来自取的学生比我们预想的多。

examples.en: In our post-decision review, we compared the original demand forecast with the actual bookings.
examples.zh: 在「决策后复盘」中，我们把原先的需求预测与真实预约数作了比较。

collocations: discuss findings from a post-decision review

words.enDefinition: a contest in which teams analyse a business case and present their recommendations to judges

examples.en: Our team entered a case competition held by two local universities in early spring.
examples.zh: 我们团队报名参加了两所当地大学在初春举办的「商业案例竞赛」。

examples.en: The case competition asked students to find a way to keep a repair shop open.
examples.zh: 「商业案例竞赛」要求学生想办法让一家维修店继续经营。

words.enDefinition: the time when competition organisers make the case materials available to teams

examples.en: The organisers postponed the case release time so teams in other time zones could participate.
examples.zh: 组织者推迟了「案例材料公布时间」，让其他时区的团队也能参加。

examples.en: We checked the case release time before booking a room for our preparation session.
examples.zh: 我们预订备赛用房间前，查看了「案例材料公布时间」。

words.enDefinition: a document giving participants a contest's task, requirements and key deadlines

examples.en: The competition brief said we could use information from the exhibits and the case narrative.
examples.zh: 「竞赛任务说明」写了我们可以用案例图表附件和正文里的信息。

examples.en: I read the competition brief twice because the slide limit was lower than I expected.
examples.zh: 幻灯片页数上限比我预期低，我把「竞赛任务说明」读了两遍。

words.enDefinition: the fixed amount of time participants are given to prepare for a task

examples.en: We used our allocated prep time to read the case and build a simple chart.
examples.zh: 我们用「分配到的准备时间」阅读案例，做了一张简单的图。

examples.en: The teams had the same allocated prep time regardless of their presentation time that afternoon.
examples.zh: 无论当天下午几点演示，各队「分配到的准备时间」都一样。

collocations: finish within the allocated prep time
make good use of the allocated prep time

words.enDefinition: a talk that explains a case analysis and any decision or recommendation for the situation

examples.en: Our case presentation led with the decision and used one table to explain the costs.
examples.zh: 我们的「案例陈述」先给出决定，再用一张表解释成本。

examples.en: The instructor asked us to link each recommendation in our case presentation to specific evidence.
examples.zh: 导师请我们把「案例陈述」中的每项建议都和具体证据对应起来。

words.enDefinition: questions a panel asks participants to understand or test the reasoning behind their entry

examples.en: The judges' questions focused on the risks that we had mentioned in our final slide.
examples.zh: 「评审提问」主要围绕我们在最后一页幻灯片上提到的风险。

examples.en: We took turns answering the judges' questions so each person could explain their own analysis.
examples.zh: 我们轮流回答「评审提问」，让每个人都能解释自己做的分析。

words.enDefinition: the last assigned period in a schedule for giving a presentation

examples.en: Our final presentation slot was just before the judges left the room to compare scores.
examples.zh: 「最后一场展示时段」是我们的，讲完后评审就离场去核对分数。

examples.en: The organisers gave the final presentation slot to the team whose train had arrived late.
examples.zh: 组织者把「最后一场展示时段」让给了火车晚点的那一队。

words.enDefinition: a group responsible for reviewing and scoring entries or performances in a competition

examples.en: The judging panel included a local shop owner and two lecturers from the business school.
examples.zh: 「评审团」有一位本地店主和两名商学院讲师。

examples.en: We gave the judging panel a short explanation of how we had estimated repair demand.
examples.zh: 我们向「评审团」简要介绍了维修需求的估算方法。

words.enDefinition: a written account of a case analysis completed by one student

examples.en: My individual case write-up explained why I had ruled out the cheaper of the two premises.
examples.zh: 我的「个人案例分析报告」解释了为什么排除两个铺位中较便宜的那个。

examples.en: The tutor asked for an individual case write-up before we presented our group conclusions.
examples.zh: 导师要求我们在陈述小组结论之前提交「个人案例分析报告」。

words.enDefinition: the work a team hands in after analysing a case together

examples.en: Our group case submission included a chart explaining how we had compared the three locations.
examples.zh: 我们的「小组提交的案例作业」里有一张图，说明我们如何比较这三个地点。

examples.en: I checked the group case submission to make sure everyone had added their references.
examples.zh: 我检查了「小组提交的案例作业」，确保每个人都加上了自己的参考资料。

collocations: hand in the group case submission

words.enDefinition: an assessment guide stating what parts of a case response are scored and how

examples.en: The case scoring rubric gave extra weight to explaining the consequences of each possible decision.
examples.zh: 「案例评分标准表」给解释各项决策后果这一项设了更高权重。

examples.en: We compared our recommendation with the case scoring rubric before submitting the final slides.
examples.zh: 提交最终的幻灯片之前，我们把建议与「案例评分标准表」作了核对。

words.enDefinition: a learning exercise that models an organisation so participants can test decisions and observe results

examples.en: We used a management simulation to see how reducing staff hours affected our ability to serve customers.
examples.zh: 我们通过「经营管理模拟」观察，缩短员工工时会怎样影响接待顾客的能力。

examples.en: The management simulation showed the effect of several teams changing their prices during the same period.
examples.zh: 「经营管理模拟」展示了多个团队在同一时期调整价格所产生的影响。

collocations: take part in a management simulation

words.enDefinition: a stage of a simulation in which participants make decisions and receive updated results

examples.en: In the first simulation round, we changed prices but kept the same number of workers.
examples.zh: 在第一轮「模拟」中，我们调了价格，员工人数保持原样。

examples.en: The next simulation round began after all teams had reviewed their results from the previous week.
examples.zh: 各队看完前一周的成绩后，下一轮「模拟」开始了。

words.enDefinition: a display grouping important data, controls or results for participants in a simulation

examples.en: We checked the simulation dashboard to see whether the delayed orders had reached the collection point.
examples.zh: 我们看了「模拟演练仪表板」，确认延误的订单有没有到自取点。

examples.en: The simulation dashboard showed each team's inventory and number of orders for the current round.
examples.zh: 「模拟演练仪表板」显示当前这轮各队的库存和订单量。

words.enDefinition: a value entered in a simulation to represent a choice controlled by the participant

examples.en: We entered the new price as a decision input before running the simulation a second time.
examples.zh: 第二次运行模拟前，我们把新价格作为「决策输入项」填了进去。

examples.en: We entered the number of workers assigned to repairs as a decision input for Saturday.
examples.zh: 我们把周六安排去维修的人数作为「决策输入项」填了进去。

words.enDefinition: an outcome produced by a simulation after running it with particular decisions or settings

examples.en: The simulation result showed lower revenue than we expected for the shop's longer opening hours.
examples.zh: 「模拟结果」显示，店铺延长营业时间后的收入低于我们预期。

examples.en: One simulation result changed when we adjusted only the number of people assigned to packing.
examples.zh: 只调整打包人手后，就有一项「模拟结果」变了。

collocations: compare a simulation result with a forecast

words.enDefinition: a discussion after a simulation to examine decisions, results and lessons

examples.en: The simulation debrief asked us to explain why we had made the first price change.
examples.zh: 在「模拟演练复盘」中，我们需要解释为什么作出第一次价格调整。

examples.en: Our team used the simulation debrief to compare its approach with the two other groups.
examples.zh: 团队借「模拟演练复盘」把自己的办法与另外两组的做法作了对比。

collocations: take notes during a simulation debrief

words.zhGloss: 把预测值和结果作比较
words.enDefinition: to check how well predicted outcomes match outcomes that are observed or produced
acceptedZhAnswers: 把预测值和结果作比较

examples.en: We stayed after the simulation to compare forecasts with results for both of our shops.
examples.zh: 模拟结束后我们留下来，对两家店都「把预测值和结果作比较」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to compare forecasts with results before explaining why the difference mattered.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先「把预测值和结果作比较」，再解释差异为什么重要。

collocations: compare forecasts with results each week
learn to compare forecasts with results
use a chart to compare forecasts with results

words.enDefinition: a factor deliberately held constant to keep its changes from influencing a comparison

examples.en: We kept the shipping charge as a control variable while comparing demand at three different prices.
examples.zh: 我们比较三个价位的需求时，把运费设为「控制变量」，保持不变。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain why total staffing hours were a control variable in the simulation.
examples.zh: 导师请我们解释，为什么员工总工时是模拟中的「控制变量」。

words.enDefinition: a value or setting used to define conditions in a scenario, often set by the person building the model

examples.en: The tutor asked why we used winter demand as the main scenario input for the exercise.
examples.zh: 导师问，我们为什么把冬季需求作为这道题的主要「情景分析输入项」。

examples.en: We set lower Saturday demand as a scenario input while keeping the team's chosen price unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们把较低的周六需求量设为「情景分析输入项」，团队选的价格原样保留。

words.enDefinition: a reference scenario whose results are used to compare the results of other scenarios

examples.en: We used the shop's current opening hours as our benchmark scenario for comparing the three alternatives.
examples.zh: 我们把店铺现有营业时间作为「基准对照情景」，用来比较另外三种方案。

examples.en: The benchmark scenario made it clear how many more orders the new proposal could handle.
examples.zh: 「基准对照情景」让人看清新方案能多处理多少订单。

collocations: compare results with a benchmark scenario

words.enDefinition: a table showing how a calculated result changes across different input values

examples.en: The sensitivity table showed operating costs at three different levels of demand for the service.
examples.zh: 「敏感性分析表」列出了三种服务需求量下的运营成本。

examples.en: We used a sensitivity table to see which changes in rent would alter our recommendation.
examples.zh: 我们用「敏感性分析表」检查，租金发生哪些变化会影响建议。

collocations: compare values in a sensitivity table

words.enDefinition: a result measured in terms other than money, such as time, quality or customer experience

examples.en: Waiting time was a nonfinancial outcome we considered when comparing plans for the repair shop.
examples.zh: 等候时长是比较维修店方案时，我们考虑的一项「非财务结果」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to mention one nonfinancial outcome alongside the forecast change in revenue.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在预测收入变化之外，再提到一项「非财务结果」。

words.enDefinition: a person with deep knowledge or practical experience in a particular subject

examples.en: We asked a subject matter expert whether the repair estimate included time for inspecting each bicycle.
examples.zh: 我们请教一位「领域专家」，维修用时的估算是否包含逐辆检查自行车的时间。

examples.en: The subject matter expert explained which costs usually changed when a shop extended its hours.
examples.zh: 「领域专家」说明了店铺延长营业时间时哪些成本通常会变。

words.enDefinition: the facts or evidence that someone could access when making a past decision

examples.en: We read only the information available at the time before choosing what to recommend to the shop.
examples.zh: 为店铺选建议方案前，我们只看了「当时能掌握的信息」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the decision was reasonable given the information available at the time.
examples.zh: 导师问，考虑到「当时能掌握的信息」，那个决定是否合理。

collocations: based on the information available at the time
review the information available at the time
act on the information available at the time

words.enDefinition: the mistake of continuing an activity because resources have already been spent despite weak future prospects

examples.en: The sunk cost fallacy kept the shop using the unpopular stand because it had already bought it.
examples.zh: 店铺因为展台已经买下就继续使用，即使它不受欢迎，这就是「沉没成本谬误」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed the sunk cost fallacy after a team proposed keeping a machine nobody used.
examples.zh: 有组建议保留没人用的机器，导师接着讨论了「沉没成本谬误」。

collocations: an example of the sunk cost fallacy
fall for the sunk cost fallacy

words.enDefinition: information that counts against a claim or assumption instead of supporting it

examples.en: We looked for disconfirming evidence before accepting the owner's explanation for the fall in sales.
examples.zh: 相信店主对销量下降的解释前，我们先找了「反驳该解释的证据」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether any disconfirming evidence appeared in the tables attached to the case.
examples.zh: 导师问，案例附表里有没有「反驳假设的证据」。

words.enDefinition: an exercise that starts by imagining a project has already failed and works backwards to identify possible causes

examples.en: We ran a premortem by assuming the evening pickup trial had already failed and asking why.
examples.zh: 我们做了「项目失败预演」，先假设晚间取货试点已经失败，再找原因。

examples.en: The premortem identified late deliveries as a risk the team had not discussed before.
examples.zh: 「项目失败预演」找出了一项团队此前没讨论过的风险，即送货延迟。

collocations: discuss the findings from a premortem

words.enDefinition: a consequence that follows from an earlier consequence rather than directly from the original action

examples.en: Shorter queues freed up the entrance, and a second-order effect was easier access for nearby shops.
examples.zh: 队伍缩短后不再堵着入口，「间接后续影响」是附近店铺更容易进出了。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify a second-order effect before recommending that the shop lower prices.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先找出一个「间接后续影响」，再建议那家店降价。

words.enDefinition: an examination of two or more cases to explain similarities and differences in choices or outcomes

examples.en: Our comparative case analysis explored why two similar shops chose quite different opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们的「比较案例分析」探讨，两家相像的店为什么选了差别很大的营业时间。

examples.en: The comparative case analysis helped us separate local constraints from challenges that both businesses faced.
examples.zh: 「比较案例分析」帮我们区分了各地特有的限制和两家都面临的困难。

collocations: findings from a comparative case analysis
